Why it is the best next use of budget: it builds on the strongest result so far while answering a broad design question in a clean way. Changing the encoder or adding fusion now would answer a narrower question or vary several choices at once.

This experiment keeps the best configuration (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000) and changes only avgpool to transformer, which isolates the effect of the aggregation method. That makes it a cheap, clean exploitation step. Its result will tell us which aggregation to carry into later encoder and multimodal comparisons, so it is a good use of the limited budget before those choices multiply the search space.

We do not yet know whether image features add complementary signal or only add noise. This experiment adds ResNet50 images to the best known setup (PCA, multiprofile, avgpool) using simple concat fusion, changing a single factor relative to config_002. If it beats 0.688, the multimodal branch is worth exploring further, including weighted fusion and ViT-L. If it does not, we can deprioritize much of the multimodal space and spend the remaining budget on RNA encoders such as scGPT. That makes it the most uncertainty-reducing experiment for the budget.

ResNet50 image-only was weak (0.227), and adding it by concat fusion lowered performance to 0.532. scGPT, the third RNA encoder, is still untested in the strongest setting. 2) This experiment changes only the RNA encoder from the current best (config_002), swapping PCA for scGPT while keeping multiprofile and avgpool. It completes the encoder comparison and shows whether a pretrained foundation-model embedding beats PCA. 3) This is a clean one-factor test on the strongest RNA-only setting, so it can either produce a new best model or confirm that PCA is the right RNA backbone. Either result guides later multimodal tests. Those would more sensibly try weighted fusion or the ViT-L image encoder on top of the best RNA encoder, rather than spend more budget on combinations that keep the weak image branch now.

It is unclear whether multimodal fails because image features carry little signal or because naive concatenation lets noisy image features dilute the strong RNA signal. 2. If it stays near 0.53 or below, ResNet50 image features likely hurt regardless of fusion, which argues for trying ViT-L or focusing on RNA-only. 3. Why now: with a limited budget, this one controlled comparison decides whether the large multimodal part of the search space deserves further experiments, while staying anchored to the best-performing RNA setup.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: The best result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (config_002, acc 0.688). With PCA, it lowered accuracy from 0.688 to 0.650. Two things remain unclear: whether the weighted-fusion advantage is general, and whether images ever add value to RNA. 2. What this tests: config_031 adds ResNet50 images with weighted fusion to the scVI multiprofile avgpool model (config_005, acc 0.635). That is a single-change comparison against config_005, isolating whether images help an scVI RNA branch. It also differs from config_019 only in the RNA encoder, which shows whether the weighted-fusion gain carries over across RNA encoders. 3. Why it is the best use of budget: It reuses the strongest known settings (multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) and has a realistic chance of a competitive score. It also directly reduces uncertainty about the central question of whether multimodal fusion beats RNA-only. Each outcome is informative: a gain over 0.635 would support pursuing fusion further, while a drop would strengthen the case for RNA-only modeling.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: scGPT RNA-only (config_007) is clearly the best result so far (acc 0.586, F1 0.574). Evidence: we have only two single-profile baselines. RNA (PCA) reached 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1. Image (ResNet50) reached 0.619 accuracy and 0.610 F1. 1) Evidence: RNA-only with PCA reached 0.678 accuracy and image-only with ResNet50 reached 0.619. Concat fusion of those same two encoders collapsed to 0.224 accuracy and 0.184 F1, far below either single modality. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only multiprofile PCA with avgpool (0.639 accuracy, 0.620 F1). PCA beat scVI and scGPT, and avgpool beat the transformer. Adding ResNet50 image features lowered performance (concat 0.535, weighted 0.512). This is likely because ResNet50 images alone are weak (0.227). The ImageNet ViT-L encoder is the largest untested design axis, so we cannot yet tell whether multimodal fusion fails in general or only with a weak image encoder. 2. Test: config_024 differs from config_018 only in the image encoder (ViT-L instead of ResNet50). It keeps the best RNA encoder, aggregation and fusion settings, so the result isolates the effect of image representation in the fusion setting. 3. Why now: Under a limited budget, this one run checks whether stronger image features help or hurt fusion, and it also has a plausible chance of beating the RNA-only best. If it still trails RNA-only, that is strong evidence to deprioritize the many remaining multimodal configurations.

1. Evidence: the best result so far is config_024 (PCA + ImageNet ViT-L, multiprofile, avgpool, concat) at 0.688 accuracy and 0.659 F1. That beats RNA-only avgpool (0.639). Multimodal fusion with ResNet50 instead hurt performance (0.535 and 0.512). This points to the image representation as the deciding factor, but no ViT-L image-only model has been run. The only image-only baseline is ResNet50 single-profile, which was weak (0.227). 2. Test: config_014 is the ViT-L image-only counterpart of config_024, keeping multiprofile and avgpool the same. It will show whether ViT-L features are strong on their own, or whether the gain in config_024 comes from them complementing PCA RNA features. 3. Why now: this isolates the image-encoder effect within the current best setting, before spending budget on fusion or aggregation variants of config_024. Its result will guide later choices, such as whether to try weighted fusion or transformer aggregation with ViT-L.

1. Evidence: Only one result exists, the RNA-only, single-profile, PCA baseline (accuracy 0.725, F1 0.685). We do not yet know how any design factor affects performance. 2. What this tests: config_002 changes only one thing, switching from single-profile to multi-profile with the simplest aggregation (avgpool), while keeping the modality and RNA encoder fixed. 1. Evidence: Only RNA-only PCA models have been tested. 1. Evidence: RNA-only with PCA is clearly stronger than image-only with ResNet50 (0.725 vs 0.532 accuracy). Multiprofile avgpool gave no gain over single-profile for RNA (0.721 vs 0.725), a gap too small to read much into. The biggest untested question is whether the image modality adds complementary signal when combined with RNA. 2. Test: config_016 is single-profile PCA RNA plus ResNet50 with simple concat fusion. It is exactly the union of the two tested single-profile unimodal baselines (config_001 and config_010), so any change from 0.725 can be attributed to adding the image modality, with no confound from aggregation or encoder choice. 3. Why now: this cleanly answers the high-impact question of whether multimodality helps, which governs most of the remaining search space. If it gains, we can then explore fusion type, image encoder and aggregation. If it does not, we can redirect the budget toward RNA encoder comparisons such as scVI and scGPT.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: RNA-only PCA is the strongest so far (0.725 single-profile, 0.721 with multiprofile avgpool). Image-only ResNet50 is weaker (0.532). 1. Evidence: RNA-only with PCA (config_001, 0.725 acc / 0.685 F1) is the best result so far. Multiprofile averaging (config_002) gave about the same result, so profile setting looks minor for now. 1. Evidence: The RNA representation has had the largest effect observed so far. In the single-profile setting, PCA_n2000 reached 0.725 accuracy and 0.685 F1, while scVI_n200 reached only 0.530 accuracy, a gap of about 0.19. Other choices mattered much less. Multiprofile avgpool was essentially equal to single-profile (0.721). Adding ResNet50 images through weighted fusion lowered accuracy to 0.688, and concat fusion failed at 0.208. RNA-only with PCA is the current best, and the third RNA encoder, scGPT, is completely untested. 2. Test: config_007 changes only the RNA encoder to scGPT, keeping rna_only and single-profile fixed. This gives a clean comparison against config_001 (PCA) and config_004 (scVI), and shows whether a foundation-model embedding beats the current PCA baseline. 3. Value: The encoder is the design choice with the largest demonstrated impact. scGPT is the main unexplored option on the strongest modality and could raise the performance ceiling. The result also shapes the remaining budget: if scGPT wins, the multiprofile and multimodal scGPT variants become the priority; if it loses, PCA is confirmed and the budget can go to aggregation (transformer) or the ViT-L image encoder. Aggregation and fusion changes have so far shown small or negative effects, so testing them first would be less informative.

This makes it the most uncertainty-reducing experiment for the remaining budget.

1. Evidence: PCA_n2000 is clearly the strongest RNA encoder, reaching 0.725 accuracy single-profile, versus about 0.53 for scVI and scGPT. Multiprofile has not helped so far: avgpool was roughly neutral at 0.721, and the transformer was clearly worse at 0.599. Among image encoders, ImageNet ViT-L beat ResNet50 (0.579 vs 0.532 accuracy, with F1 following the same pattern). In multimodal models, concat fusion collapsed to 0.208. Weighted fusion with ResNet50 reached 0.688, which is still below RNA-only. The main open question is whether any multimodal setup can beat RNA-only, or whether the weaker image signal mainly adds noise. 2. Test: config_023 keeps the best previously tested multimodal setup (single-profile, PCA_n2000, weighted fusion) and changes only the image encoder from ResNet50 to ViT-L. This isolates whether the stronger image representation improves fusion enough to close or reverse the gap to RNA-only. 3. Why now: This is a one-variable extension of the most promising multimodal result, so it combines exploitation with a clean test. It also decides whether the many remaining ViT-L multimodal configurations are worth budget. It avoids concat, which looks unstable from a single result, and avoids multiprofile aggregation, which has shown no benefit yet.

Transformer aggregation added a smaller gain (0.678 accuracy, 0.646 F1), so it is the best setting so far. The image-only ResNet50 single-profile model was weak (0.227), so it is unclear whether images will add value. 1) Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality. RNA-only reached 0.421 accuracy versus 0.227 for image-only in single-profile. Multiprofile aggregation gave large gains (pca avgpool 0.653, pca transformer 0.678 / F1 0.646, the current best). Adding ResNet50 images with concat fusion lowered performance to 0.599. Evidence: Multiprofile aggregation clearly helps RNA-only models (0.42 single-profile vs 0.65 avgpool and 0.68 transformer). scVI is the best RNA encoder so far (0.725). Images alone are weak (ResNet50 0.227). Adding ResNet50 images through concat fusion lowered accuracy from 0.678 to 0.599 (config_003 vs config_020). That drop is a single result, so it is unclear whether multimodality itself hurts or whether concat fusion lets a noisy image signal degrade the RNA representation. Test: config_021 is identical to config_020 except that it uses weighted fusion instead of concat. This isolates the effect of the fusion method, and it can show whether weighted fusion learns to down-weight the weak image branch and recover or exceed RNA-only performance. Why now: The answer decides how to spend much of the remaining budget, since most untested configurations are multimodal. If weighted fusion still underperforms RNA-only, we can largely drop multimodal ResNet50 options and focus on scVI-based RNA models or test a stronger image encoder. If it helps, scVI with weighted fusion becomes a logical next step.

1) Evidence: Multiprofile aggregation clearly helps, roughly +0.23 to +0.25 accuracy over single-profile for PCA RNA, and transformer aggregation slightly beats avgpool. Among RNA encoders, scVI is the strongest so far (0.725 vs 0.678 for PCA under the same transformer setting), while scGPT is poor. Adding ResNet50 images with weighted fusion improved the PCA transformer model (0.713/0.695 vs 0.678/0.646), whereas concat fusion hurt it (0.599). This suggests that weighted fusion lets the model use weak image signal without being dragged down by it. 2) Test: config_033 changes only the RNA encoder from config_021 (PCA to scVI). It also differs from the current best, config_006, only by adding ResNet50 images with weighted fusion. So it shows whether the fusion gain seen with PCA carries over to the stronger scVI representation, or whether scVI already captures what images add. 3) Why now: it directly exploits the two most promising findings (scVI and weighted fusion), is the most likely candidate to beat 0.725, and cleanly isolates whether the image modality adds value, which is a central open design question.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only scVI with a transformer (0.725 acc). Fusion results are mixed. With PCA RNA, weighted fusion with ResNet50 improved over RNA-only (0.713 vs 0.678, F1 0.695 vs 0.646), and weighted beat concat (0.599). With scVI RNA, the same weighted fusion with ResNet50 fell sharply (0.530). The image encoder is the largest untested design dimension: every image run used ResNet50, which is weak on its own (0.227 single-profile). 2. Test: config_027 keeps everything from config_021 (PCA, multiprofile, transformer, weighted fusion) and changes only the image encoder to ImageNet ViT-L. This isolates whether a stronger image representation adds more complementary signal in the fusion setup that has worked best so far. 3. Why now: It is a one-variable change from a strong multimodal baseline, so it is both exploitative and directly informative. A gain would justify exploring ViT-L further, including retrying scVI fusion. No gain would suggest image features add little and point the search back toward RNA-only refinement.

Adding images to single-profile PCA lowered accuracy to 0.629. Multiprofile avgpool lowered RNA-only accuracy to 0.653, but its effect on the multimodal model is untested. 2. Test: config_018 combines the strongest component at each axis (PCA, ResNet50, concat, avgpool) in a multiprofile multimodal model. It checks whether pooling across profiles can reduce noise in the weak image signal enough for fusion to help rather than hurt. 3. Why this is the best final choice: the remaining RNA-only options all use scVI or scGPT, which were clearly weaker (about 0.51–0.52), so they are very unlikely to reach 0.72. Config_018 still probably falls short of 0.721, but among the untested configurations it is the most plausible candidate to beat the current best.

Why it is the best use of the last experiment: only the best accuracy counts, and config_007 is already secured. A higher-variance extension of the strongest direction is therefore preferable to config_008 (avgpool), whose expected gain from prior evidence is near zero. It is also preferable to scVI or ViT-L options, which have no supporting evidence or performed poorly.

Multiprofile avgpool (0.639) and the ViT-L encoder (0.525) also underperformed the ResNet50 single-profile baseline. 2) Test: config_017 keeps the multimodal concat setup (PCA + ResNet50, single profile) and changes only concat to weighted fusion. If weighted fusion still trails image-only, the remaining budget can go to image-side variants such as transformer aggregation (config_012) or better RNA encoders.

1) Evidence: The image_only resnet50 setup is the strongest so far. Singleprofile reached 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1. Multiprofile with avgpool aggregation was somewhat lower at 0.639. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_016 (PCA + ResNet50, single-profile, concat) at 0.540 accuracy and 0.524 F1. Image-only ResNet50 is close behind at 0.535, so RNA adds only a little. Evidence: multiprofile with transformer aggregation (config_020: pca_n2000 + resnet50 + concat) is clearly the best result at 0.650 accuracy and 0.628 F1. That is far above every other run. Avgpool aggregation did not produce the same gain (0.525). Among the single-component alternatives, ImageNet ViT-L was only slightly below resnet50 in the singleprofile setting (0.530 vs 0.540). Weighted fusion was a larger step down (0.523 vs 0.540). The scVI and scGPT RNA encoders collapsed performance, so they are poor bets. Test: this run keeps the winning recipe (multiprofile, transformer aggregation, pca_n2000, concat) and changes only the image encoder to ViT-L. It asks whether richer ViT-L features gain more from transformer aggregation across profiles than resnet50 did. Why this is the best final experiment: with no budget left, the only thing that counts is the chance of beating 0.650. A one-factor change to the best configuration, using the alternative with the smallest observed penalty, seems more likely to match or beat it than switching fusion, RNA encoder, or dropping a modality.

1) Evidence: only one result exists so far. The RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline (config_001) reached 0.328 accuracy and 0.288 F1. 1) Evidence: single-profile RNA-only PCA is the best result so far (0.629). Multiprofile aggregation clearly hurt PCA (0.507 with avgpool, 0.421 with transformer). Weighted fusion and the ViT-L image encoder also performed poorly. Concat fusion with ResNet50 was the least harmful multimodal choice (0.536). Among RNA encoders, scGPT was second best (0.573) and had the most balanced F1 (0.573), suggesting a robust representation. 2) Test: this run checks whether scGPT pairs better with ResNet50 image features than PCA did under the least harmful fusion setup, concat in single-profile mode. That isolates the RNA-encoder-by-fusion interaction. 3) Rationale: this is the last experiment, so the goal is the best remaining chance of beating 0.629. Every other untested option uses a component that has already performed poorly (multiprofile aggregation, ViT-L or weighted fusion). This configuration avoids all of them while testing an untried combination. It is unlikely, but plausible, that it exceeds the PCA baseline.

1. There is no evidence yet, so every design choice is uncertain: modality, profile setting, RNA and image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. 2. This run sets a mid-complexity anchor: multimodal, multiprofile, PCA RNA plus ResNet50 image features, average pooling and concat fusion. Each component is the simplest option within its type. Almost every single-factor ablation is available next: RNA-only (config_002), image-only (config_011), single-profile (config_016), transformer aggregation (config_020), weighted fusion (config_019), and alternative RNA or image encoders (config_030, config_024). 3. With only 10 runs, a central configuration that can plausibly score well gives a baseline to compare against. It lets the next experiments isolate one factor at a time, rather than starting from the weakest corner of the search space.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: We have only one result. The multimodal, multiprofile configuration (PCA RNA + ResNet50 image, avgpool, concat) reached 0.421 accuracy and 0.412 F1. That gives a baseline but says nothing yet about which design choices matter. 2. What this tests: config_024 keeps everything the same except the image encoder, swapping ResNet50 for ImageNet ViT-L. Because only one factor changes, any difference can be attributed to the image representation. 3. Why it is the best next use of the budget: The image encoder is one of the main representation choices, and a stronger pretrained encoder could plausibly raise accuracy. If ViT-L helps, later experiments can build on it; if it does not, we keep ResNet50 and move on to other factors such as RNA encoder, aggregation or profile setting. A modality ablation (RNA-only, config_002) would also have been reasonable, since we do not yet know how much the image branch contributes. That remains a useful check later.

1) Evidence: with everything else held fixed (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool, concat), switching the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l raised validation accuracy from 0.421 to 0.639, and F1 rose similarly. That makes the image encoder the strongest signal so far. Aggregation, fusion, RNA encoder and the value of multiprofile input are all still untested. 2) This experiment keeps the best configuration (config_024) and changes only the aggregation, from avgpool to transformer. It tests whether learned attention across multiple profiles beats simple mean pooling when paired with the stronger image features. 3) It is a single-factor change around the current best, so it can both improve the result and cleanly isolate an important design choice. Later experiments can test fusion (weighted), RNA encoders (scvi or scgpt) and image-only or single-profile baselines against this anchor.

1) Evidence: The image encoder matters a lot. Swapping resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l raised accuracy from 0.421 to 0.639, and F1 rose with it. Under vit_l, avgpool clearly beat transformer aggregation (0.639 vs 0.485). The RNA encoder is still completely untested: every run so far used pca_n2000. 2) This experiment keeps the best configuration (config_024: multiprofile, vit_l, avgpool, concat) and changes only the RNA encoder, from pca_n2000 to scvi_n200. That isolates the effect of the RNA representation. 3) RNA encoder is the largest unexplored design dimension, with three options. A single-variable test against the current best both reduces that uncertainty and could directly beat 0.639. If scvi helps, scgpt (config_048) is the natural next comparison. If it does not, later runs can refine fusion (weighted, config_025) on the pca setup or check RNA's contribution with image-only vit_l (config_014).

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_024 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + concat) at 0.639 accuracy and 0.620 F1. Three single-factor changes from it each hurt badly. Swapping to resnet50 gave 0.421. Swapping to transformer aggregation gave 0.485. Swapping to scvi_n200 gave 0.260. Fusion is the one design choice not yet tested. 2. Test: config_025 changes only concat to weighted fusion and keeps everything else from the best configuration. This isolates the effect of fusion. The large scVI drop suggests the way RNA and image signals are combined matters a lot, so a learned weighting could balance the modalities better than concatenation. 3. Why now: This is the most direct, low-risk extension of the strongest configuration. It resolves an untested design axis and has a real chance of beating 0.639. Five experiments remain after it, leaving room to later check image-only or scgpt variants.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_025 (PCA RNA, ViT-L image, avgpool, weighted fusion) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. Three choices look consistent: ViT-L clearly beat ResNet50 under concat, avgpool beat transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion beat concat by about 8 points. The RNA encoder is still uncertain. scVI was much worse than PCA (0.26 vs 0.64 under concat), and scGPT has never been tested. 2. Test: This keeps the best image encoder, aggregation and fusion and changes only the RNA encoder to scGPT. It shows directly whether a foundation-model RNA embedding beats PCA in the strongest setup. 3. Why now: The RNA encoder is the main untested design axis that could raise the top score. Changing one variable from the best configuration keeps the comparison clean. With 4 experiments left, it is a reasonable bet: a cheaper check than broad exploration, with real upside if scGPT outperforms PCA.

Evidence: the best result so far is config_025 (PCA_n2000 + ViT-L, multiprofile avgpool, weighted fusion) at 0.721 accuracy. Swapping ResNet50 for ViT-L raised accuracy by about 0.22, while scVI and scGPT RNA encoders both performed much worse than PCA. This suggests the image representation carries much of the signal. Weighted fusion beat concat by about 0.08, which may mean the model gains from down-weighting a weaker RNA branch. The main open question is whether RNA adds anything beyond ViT-L image features. This experiment runs the image-only model with ViT-L and multiprofile avgpool, which changes only the model setting relative to the best configuration. It shows whether multimodality truly helps or whether image-only could match or beat 0.721. With 3 experiments left, settling this modality question first decides where the remaining budget goes: refining multimodal fusion and profile setting, or exploiting image-only variants.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_025 (PCA RNA, ViT-L image, multiprofile avgpool, weighted fusion) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. Weighted fusion beat concat on this setup (0.721 vs 0.639). ViT-L clearly beat ResNet50, and PCA clearly beat scVI and scGPT. Transformer aggregation hurt (0.485 vs 0.639 with concat). The singleprofile setting has never been tested, so it is the largest open uncertainty. 2. Test: config_023 keeps the best configuration's RNA encoder, image encoder and weighted fusion, and changes only the profile setting to singleprofile. This isolates whether multiprofile aggregation actually helps, or whether avgpool over profiles dilutes the signal. 3. Why now: Retrying the transformer (config_027) or ResNet (config_019) is unlikely to pay off given the poor results for both. This single-variable change has a real chance of beating 0.721. Either way, the result tells me how to use the final two experiments.

1. Evidence: the best result is config_025 (PCA-2000 + ViT-L, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) at 0.721 accuracy. Image-only ViT-L with the same profile setting and aggregation reached only 0.532, and the concat version of the multimodal model reached 0.639. So the PCA RNA features seem to drive much of the gain, especially when weighted fusion can adjust how much each modality counts. The transformer aggregator cut accuracy sharply (0.639 to 0.485), ResNet50 underperformed ViT-L, and scVI and scGPT were much worse than PCA. 2. Test: config_002 isolates the PCA RNA representation under the best profile and aggregation settings (multiprofile, avgpool), with no image branch. This shows whether the image branch adds value or whether RNA alone can match or beat the multimodal model. 3. Why now: this removes the largest remaining uncertainty and has a realistic chance of a new best. It also leaves one experiment to exploit whichever direction wins, either refining the multimodal model or pursuing RNA-only.

1) Evidence: the best result so far is config_025 (PCA-2000 + ViT-L, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted fusion) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. Weighted fusion beat concat by about 0.08 accuracy with the same backbone (0.721 vs 0.639). The other alternatives look weaker under concat: scVI (0.260) and ResNet50 (0.421). scGPT was also weak even with weighted fusion (0.427). The main open question is aggregation. Transformer aggregation hurt under concat (0.485 vs 0.639), but it has never been tested with weighted fusion. 2) Test: config_027 changes only aggregation relative to the best configuration, swapping avgpool for transformer. This checks whether weighted fusion lets the transformer aggregator work better than it did under concat. 3) Why this is the best final experiment: only the best accuracy counts, so the last run should go to the option with a realistic chance of beating 0.721. Every other untested choice changes a component (encoder or backbone) that has clearly underperformed. Transformer aggregation's poor result comes from a single run, so it is the least settled of those weak components. Isolating it on the strongest setup is the best remaining shot at exceeding 0.721, even though it is more likely to fall short.

1. Evidence: no experiments have been run, so we know nothing yet about which modality, encoder, profile setting, aggregation or fusion helps. 2. Test: config_001 (RNA-only, single profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest configuration in the space. It sets a reference accuracy and F1 that later results can be compared against. Why now: with 10 experiments, an early simple reference is the cheapest way to cut uncertainty and avoid over-reading results from complex multimodal or multiprofile models. 1) Evidence: The only result so far is the single-profile RNA baseline (PCA-2000), with accuracy 0.573 and F1 0.573. We do not yet know how informative the image modality is by itself, and that is the biggest open question about the search space. 2) Test: config_010 runs the single-profile image-only model with ResNet50 under the same setting as config_001. Only the modality changes, so the result gives a clean RNA-vs-image comparison. 3) Why now: About two-thirds of the remaining configurations are multimodal or image-based. Knowing whether images are competitive, complementary, or weak will tell us whether to spend the remaining 8 experiments on image encoders and fusion or on RNA encoders and multiprofile aggregation. One result will not settle this, but it sharpens later decisions more than tuning RNA settings first.

1) Evidence: two single-profile baselines so far. RNA-only with pca_n2000 (acc 0.573) clearly beats image-only with resnet50 (acc 0.422). Neither the profile setting nor fusion has been tested yet. 2) Test: config_016 adds resnet50 image features to the same pca_n2000 RNA setup using simple concat fusion, staying single-profile. Both encoders are unchanged from the tested baselines, so the only difference is combining the two modalities. This isolates whether adding the weaker image modality helps or hurts relative to the 0.573 RNA-only result. 3) Why now: whether multimodal fusion adds value is the design question that splits most of the remaining configurations, and the experiment is cleanly controlled against both completed runs. Its answer will decide whether to spend the remaining 7 runs on multimodal variants (multiprofile aggregation, weighted fusion, other encoders) or on RNA-only refinements such as scvi, scgpt and multiprofile aggregation.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: RNA-only with PCA (0.573) is the best result so far. Image-only ResNet50 is much weaker (0.422). Concat fusion of the two (0.542, F1 0.483) did worse than RNA alone, so the image signal currently seems to add noise rather than help. Profile setting has not been tested at all, and it could be a large lever. 2. What this tests: config_002 keeps the best configuration fixed (RNA-only, PCA n2000) and changes only singleprofile to multiprofile, using simple avgpool aggregation. This isolates the effect of the profile setting without confounding it with encoder or fusion changes. 3. Why it is the best next use of budget: multiprofile applies across most of the remaining search space, so its effect should be established early. If it helps, later experiments can test transformer aggregation and alternative RNA encoders (scVI, scGPT) in the multiprofile setting. If it does not, the remaining budget can go to RNA encoder comparisons in singleprofile.

1. Evidence: RNA carries most of the signal so far. RNA-only single-profile PCA gave the best accuracy (0.573 accuracy, 0.573 F1). Image-only ResNet50 was much weaker (0.422). Adding ResNet50 images via concat fusion lowered accuracy (0.542), with a larger drop in F1 (0.483). Moving to multiprofile avgpool also lowered results (0.540). The largest untested factor is the RNA encoder, since only PCA has been tried. 2. Test: config_004 swaps PCA for scVI in the best setup (RNA-only, single-profile) and changes nothing else. This isolates the effect of RNA representation on the strongest branch. 3. Why now: RNA representation looks like the main lever, so it is the most likely route to a higher best accuracy. The result also tells us which RNA encoder to carry into later aggregation or fusion experiments. scGPT (config_007) is the natural follow-up if scVI does not beat PCA.

1) Evidence: RNA is clearly the dominant modality. RNA-only PCA singleprofile is best at 0.573 accuracy. Image-only ResNet50 reaches only 0.422. Adding images by concat (0.542) and multiprofile avgpool (0.540) both lowered accuracy. Among RNA encoders, PCA beat scVI (0.507), but scGPT is still untested, so the RNA encoder choice remains the largest open question. 2) Test: config_007 changes only the encoder to scGPT, keeping RNA-only and singleprofile. This isolates the encoder effect against the current best. 3) Why now: if scGPT beats PCA, it would likely carry into the remaining multimodal and aggregation tests and could set a new best. If it loses, PCA is confirmed as the base. Then the last 3 experiments can go to weighted fusion (config_017) or transformer aggregation (config_003) built on PCA.

1) Evidence: RNA-only PCA single-profile (config_001, 0.573 accuracy) is the best result so far. The scVI and scGPT encoders, avgpool multiprofile and concat multimodal fusion all fell short of it. Concat fusion with ResNet50 (config_016) dropped to 0.542 and had a much lower F1 (0.483). The weak image branch (0.422) may be diluting the RNA signal. 2) Test: config_017 keeps config_016 identical and changes only the fusion from concat to weighted. This isolates whether a learned weighting can down-weight the weaker image modality and recover or beat RNA-only performance. 3) Why now: fusion is a key untested design choice, and the answer decides whether the remaining budget should go to multimodal variants (for example ViT-L or multiprofile weighted fusion) or to RNA-only refinements such as transformer aggregation (config_003). It is a clean one-variable comparison with real upside.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_017 (single-profile, PCA RNA + ResNet50, weighted fusion) at 0.586 accuracy and 0.574 F1. Weighted fusion clearly beat concat (0.542), and PCA was the strongest RNA encoder. The weak link looks like the image branch: ResNet50 image-only reached only 0.422, and the ImageNet ViT-L encoder has not been tested at all. Multiprofile avgpool lowered RNA-only accuracy (0.540 vs 0.573), so moving to multiprofile looks less promising right now. 2. Test: Keep everything from the best configuration and change only the image encoder to ViT-L. This isolates whether a stronger image representation raises multimodal weighted-fusion accuracy. 3. Why now: It is a single-variable extension of the current best, so it exploits the strongest direction while also answering an untested representation question. The result will guide the last two experiments, for example whether to pair the better image encoder with transformer aggregation.

1. Evidence: the best result so far is config_017 (PCA + ResNet50, singleprofile, weighted fusion) at 0.586 accuracy and 0.574 F1. Weighted fusion clearly beat concat with the same encoders (0.586 vs 0.542). PCA was the strongest RNA encoder, and ResNet50 far outperformed ViT-L when fused. The main open question is aggregation. Multiprofile avgpool hurt RNA-only accuracy (0.573 to 0.540), but transformer aggregation, which can learn to weight informative profiles instead of averaging them, has not been tested anywhere. 2. Test: config_021 keeps the best encoders and fusion fixed. It changes only the profile setting to multiprofile with transformer aggregation (these two choices come together, since aggregation only applies to multiprofile). This shows whether learned aggregation over multiple profiles can improve on the best singleprofile multimodal model. 3. Why now: with only two experiments left, exploiting the strongest direction while probing the one untested design dimension gives the best chance of a new maximum. Running the RNA-only transformer test (config_003) first would isolate the effect more cleanly, but it is unlikely to beat 0.586 itself. If config_021 underperforms, the final experiment can fall back to other variants around config_017.

1. Evidence: the best result so far is config_021 (multimodal, multiprofile, PCA + ResNet50, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) at 0.635 accuracy and 0.618 F1. Transformer aggregation appears to be the main driver of the multiprofile gain, because avgpool multiprofile hurt RNA-only (0.540 vs 0.573). PCA beat scVI and scGPT, and ResNet50 beat ViT-L by a wide margin, so swapping encoders is unlikely to help. The open question is fusion under multiprofile: concat trailed weighted in single-profile (0.542 vs 0.586), but that was without a learned aggregator. A transformer aggregator may reweight modality tokens itself and reduce the need for a fixed weighted fusion. 2. Test: this keeps every other part of the best configuration fixed and changes only fusion to concat. It isolates the fusion effect in the strongest setting. 3. Why this is the best final use: it is a one-change neighbor of the current best and keeps the components with the strongest evidence. The alternative neighbor, avgpool with weighted fusion (config_019), drops transformer aggregation, which has better support than weighted fusion does in the multiprofile setting. Concat may still underperform, as it did in single-profile, but this gives a reasonable chance of exceeding 0.635 on the last experiment.

1. Evidence: No experiments have been run yet, so we know nothing about how encoders, modalities, profile settings, aggregation or fusion perform. 2. Test: config_001 (RNA-only, single-profile, PCA-2000) is the simplest pipeline. It sets a baseline for accuracy and F1. Later experiments can then change one factor at a time against it: RNA encoder (scVI, scGPT), image-only, multiprofile aggregation, or multimodal fusion. Each gain or loss can then be attributed to a specific design choice. 3. Why now: With 9 experiments left, a clean, low-variance reference is the best first step. It prevents assuming that more complex multimodal or multiprofile models are better, and makes every later one-factor comparison easy to interpret.

1) Evidence: only one experiment has been run, the RNA-only single-profile PCA baseline, at 0.715 accuracy and 0.687 F1. We know nothing yet about the image modality, fusion, encoders or multiprofile aggregation. 2) Test: config_016 keeps the RNA encoder (PCA) and the single-profile setting fixed and adds ResNet50 image features with simple concat fusion. This isolates one design choice: whether adding images helps over the RNA-only baseline. 3) Why now: the RNA-vs-multimodal choice cuts the search space in half and decides where most of the remaining 8 experiments should go. A gain supports exploiting multimodal configurations. No gain or a loss steers the search toward RNA encoders and aggregation. Concat with ResNet50 is the simplest, lowest-risk multimodal variant, so the comparison stays clean before more complex fusion or aggregation is tried.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is the simplest model, RNA-only single-profile with the PCA encoder (config_001, acc 0.715, F1 0.687). Test: this keeps the best setup (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer) and swaps weighted fusion for concat, isolating the effect of fusion. 3. Why now: fusion is a core multimodal design choice with no evidence so far. Changing one variable around the current best both reduces that uncertainty and could directly improve the best result. 1) Evidence: pca_n2000 (0.527) and scvi_n200 (0.518) clearly beat scgpt (0.332). Weighted fusion is slightly ahead of concat (0.527 vs 0.514), and its F1 is consistent with that, but the gap is small. Every run so far used imagenet_vit_l with transformer aggregation, so aggregation and image encoder are still untested. 2) config_022 keeps the current best setup (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, weighted fusion) and changes only aggregation, from transformer to avgpool. 1. Evidence: The RNA encoder matters a lot. scGPT scored 0.33, while scVI and PCA scored about 0.52–0.53. With pca_n2000, aggregation (transformer 0.527 vs avgpool 0.525) and fusion (weighted 0.527 vs concat 0.514) made only small differences. However, every run so far used imagenet_vit_l, so the image encoder is the largest untested design choice. 2. Test: config_025 keeps the current best setup (pca_n2000, transformer, weighted) and swaps only the image encoder to resnet50. This isolates the image-encoder effect cleanly. 3. Why now: With 4 experiments left, resolving a possibly large factor is worth more than fine-tuning aggregation or fusion, which have shown small effects. If resnet50 does better, the remaining runs can exploit it. If it does worse, vit_l is confirmed and the remaining budget can go to profile setting or other refinements.

1. Evidence and uncertainty: Every experiment so far has used the multiprofile setting. Within that setting, pca_n2000 with imagenet_vit_l is the strongest pairing. The best result is config_012 (transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) at 0.527 accuracy and 0.510 F1. Avgpool aggregation was nearly tied at 0.525 accuracy. Weighted fusion slightly beat concat. ViT-L clearly beat ResNet50, and pca_n2000 and scvi_n200 clearly beat scGPT. These remaining small differences are within noise, so further tweaks to aggregation or fusion are unlikely to add much. 2. What this tests: config_030 keeps the best encoders and fusion but switches to singleprofile. This answers whether multiprofile aggregation actually helps, or whether a single-profile model matches or beats it. 3. Why now: profile setting is the largest design choice still untested. Testing it now, while 3 experiments remain, leaves room to exploit the result. If singleprofile is competitive, the remaining budget can refine it; if it is worse, multiprofile is confirmed and we can return to fine-tuning there.

1) Evidence: Within multimodal multiprofile runs, the image encoder matters most. ViT-L reached 0.513–0.527, while swapping in ResNet50 dropped accuracy to 0.471. The RNA encoder matters mainly in the negative direction: scGPT collapsed to 0.332, while PCA and scVI were close (0.527 vs 0.518). Aggregation and fusion changes made only small differences (about 0.01 or less). Further RNA, fusion or aggregation tweaks around config_012 (0.527) are therefore likely to give only marginal gains. The untested question is whether the RNA branch helps at all, since a weak RNA branch clearly can hurt. 2) Test: config_045 runs image-only ViT-L with transformer multiprofile aggregation, the strongest image setup seen so far, without RNA. If it matches or beats 0.527, the image modality dominates and unimodal or image-centric configurations become the best direction. If it falls clearly below, RNA fusion adds value and the last experiment should refine the multimodal setup, such as scVI with avgpool and weighted fusion. 3) Why now: it tests a major untested design choice (modality) that could change the best result. It also tells us how to spend the final experiment, which a small local tweak of an already near-flat region would not.

Evidence: the image-only ViT-L multiprofile transformer model (config_045, 0.629 acc, 0.599 F1) clearly beats every multimodal variant, which top out around 0.53. That suggests adding RNA features hurts this task. ViT-L beat ResNet50, multiprofile beat singleprofile by a wide margin, and avgpool vs. transformer aggregation was nearly tied in the multimodal setting (0.525 vs. 0.527). Test: config_021 keeps the strongest settings (image-only, ViT-L, multiprofile) and swaps transformer aggregation for avgpool. This checks whether simpler pooling matches or beats transformer aggregation once RNA is removed. Why now: with only two experiments left, exploiting the clearly dominant image-only ViT-L direction gives the best chance of improving the top accuracy. Aggregation is the only untested design choice within that direction, and the near-tie seen in the multimodal runs makes avgpool a credible contender.

1. Evidence: The image-only models clearly beat everything else. Image-only ViT-L with avgpool reached 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1, and with transformer aggregation 0.629. Every multimodal model stayed at or below about 0.527, so adding RNA seems to hurt. Avgpool also looks better than transformer for image-only. Single-profile input was very poor (0.224), so config_041 (image-only, single-profile) is unlikely to win. 2. What this tests: config_016 is the only untested image-only, multiprofile, avgpool configuration, differing from the best model only in using ResNet50. It checks whether a ResNet50 image backbone can match or beat ViT-L within the strongest setup found so far. 3. Why it is the best final choice: ResNet50 trailed ViT-L in the multimodal comparison (0.471 vs 0.527), so a gain is not expected. Still, with one experiment left, staying in the image-only, multiprofile, avgpool region is the most plausible chance of exceeding 0.713. Every other untested option would revisit settings that were consistently weak: RNA inclusion, single-profile input, or a weaker encoder.

1. Evidence: no experiments have been run, so the only guide is prior knowledge. Multimodal models usually beat single-modality ones. Pooling several profiles with learned aggregation tends to help. Large pretrained encoders (scGPT for RNA, ImageNet ViT-L for images) often give the most transferable features. 2. Test: config_015 combines all of these (multimodal, multiprofile, scGPT, ViT-L, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion). Why now: with only 10 runs and only the best result counting, starting from a likely high performer secures a good result early. Later runs can then make controlled one-factor changes from this anchor (e.g., concat vs weighted fusion, avgpool vs transformer, other encoders, unimodal ablations) to see which design choices matter.

1. Evidence: Only one result exists so far. The multimodal, multiprofile config with scGPT RNA, ViT-L image, transformer aggregation and weighted fusion reached 0.527 accuracy and 0.510 F1. 1) Evidence: with everything else held fixed (multimodal, multiprofile, ViT-L, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion), scGPT beat scVI by about 10 points in accuracy (0.527 vs 0.427), and F1 agrees. If PCA beats scGPT, we change direction early; if not, we exploit scGPT with more confidence.

1. Evidence: with the ViT-L, transformer and weighted-fusion backbone held fixed, scGPT (0.527 acc / 0.510 F1) and PCA-2000 (0.525 / 0.498) perform about the same. scVI-200 is clearly worse (0.427). scGPT is slightly ahead on F1, so it is a reasonable anchor. With 6 experiments left, a one-factor change on the current best is the cleanest way to settle a major design choice. It also has a real chance of beating the current best. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_005 (scGPT + ViT-L + transformer + concat, 0.629 accuracy, 0.599 F1). Transformer aggregation clearly beats avgpool (0.629 vs 0.224). Concat beats weighted fusion for scGPT (0.629 vs 0.527). scGPT and PCA performed about equally under weighted fusion, and scVI was weaker. Test: config_032 keeps the best settings (scGPT, transformer, concat) and swaps only the image encoder to ResNet50. 1. Evidence: Concat fusion beat weighted by about 0.10 with scGPT and ViT-L. Transformer aggregation beat avgpool by a wide margin. ResNet50 slightly outperformed ViT-L in the concat setting (best so far: config_032 at 0.653). The RNA encoder is the main open question. Test: config_010 keeps the best settings (multiprofile, ResNet50, transformer, concat) and swaps scGPT for PCA-2000. 1) Evidence: the best result so far is config_032 (scGPT + ResNet50 + transformer + concat, 0.653 acc / 0.628 F1). scGPT clearly beats PCA and scVI, and concat clearly beats weighted fusion (0.629 vs 0.527 with ViT-L). Aggregation choice is critical: avgpool collapsed to 0.224, while transformer worked well. However, every experiment so far has used multiprofile inputs, so profile setting is the largest untested design dimension. 2) This experiment runs the singleprofile version of the best component set (scGPT + ResNet50 + concat). It tests whether the multiprofile setup with transformer aggregation is actually needed, or whether a single profile without aggregation matches or beats it. Removing aggregation also removes the failure mode seen with avgpool. 3) The other dimensions already have reasonably clear winners, so this is the best remaining chance to find a configuration above 0.653. If it underperforms, it confirms multiprofile plus transformer. The last two experiments can then go to the RNA-only scGPT ablation or nearby variants of config_032.

1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_001 (single-profile, scGPT, ResNet50, concat) at 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1. Three choices are well supported. scGPT clearly beats PCA and scVI. Concat fusion beats weighted fusion by about 0.10. A transformer aggregator beats avgpool by a wide margin. The image encoder is the least settled choice: ResNet50 beat ViT-L by only about 0.024 in one multi-profile comparison (0.653 vs 0.629), which is too small to rule ViT-L out. 2. Test: config_047 keeps the strongest setting (single-profile, scGPT, concat) and swaps in ViT-L. Why now: With only one experiment left after this, a one-change variation of the top configuration is the best balance of exploitation and resolving the remaining open question. 1. Evidence: the best result is config_001 (single-profile, scGPT + ResNet50, concat) at 0.678 accuracy and 0.646 F1. scGPT clearly beats PCA and scVI. Concat beat weighted fusion by about 0.10 in the one direct comparison, which makes config_025 (weighted fusion) unlikely to win. The image encoder also mattered a lot: ViT-L scored about 0.54 versus 0.68 for ResNet50. The open question is whether images help at all or whether a weaker image branch mainly adds noise. 2. Test: config_046 trains scGPT alone, single-profile with no image branch. It is the one untested variant of the top setup that could plausibly exceed it, if the RNA embedding carries most of the signal. 3. Why this experiment: with one run left, the other options either use weaker RNA encoders (PCA, scVI), weighted fusion, or multi-profile aggregation, all of which have underperformed. Isolating the strongest component (scGPT, single-profile) is the most credible remaining shot at a higher accuracy. It also shows how much the image modality actually contributes.

1) No experiments have been run yet, so we have no evidence on modality, profile setting, encoders, aggregation or fusion. Priors favor multimodal inputs, multiprofile context and stronger encoders as the likeliest route to high accuracy. 2) config_007 tests a strong 'full-capacity' anchor: multimodal, multiprofile, scVI RNA embeddings, ImageNet ViT-L image features, transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. 1. Evidence: Only one result exists. The full multimodal setup (multiprofile, scVI-200, ViT-L, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) reached 0.208 accuracy and 0.172 F1. This gives no information yet about which components drive performance, and the most basic open question is whether the image branch adds value. 2. What this tests: config_040 keeps the same profile setting, RNA encoder and transformer aggregation but drops the image modality. It is therefore a one-factor ablation of multimodality against config_007. If RNA-only matches or beats 0.208, the search should focus on the RNA encoder and aggregation choices. If it falls clearly below, the image features matter, and later experiments should explore image encoder and fusion variants. 3. Why now: With 8 experiments left, settling the modality question first prunes a large part of the space, since 39 of the 50 untested configurations are multimodal. 1) Evidence: with everything else fixed (multiprofile, scVI, transformer), RNA-only reached 0.494 accuracy (F1 0.453), while adding ViT-L images with weighted fusion dropped to 0.208. So the RNA branch carries most of the signal, and this image fusion setup hurts. The RNA encoder choice is still untested. 2) Test: config_006 keeps the best setup (RNA-only, multiprofile, transformer) and changes only the encoder from scVI to scGPT. This shows whether a pretrained foundation-model embedding beats scVI. 3) Value: the RNA representation is likely the largest remaining lever on accuracy within the best direction so far. A one-variable change keeps the result easy to read. Later experiments can then try avgpool aggregation, PCA, or concat fusion on the winning encoder.

1) Evidence: scGPT is clearly the strongest RNA encoder so far. scGPT RNA-only with multiprofile and transformer reached 0.678 accuracy, versus 0.494 for scVI. The only multimodal run (scVI + ViT-L, transformer, weighted fusion) collapsed to 0.208, well below its RNA-only counterpart. So we do not yet know whether adding images can help, or whether that failure came from weighted fusion. 2) This run keeps the best RNA setup (scGPT, multiprofile, transformer) and adds ViT-L images with concat fusion instead of weighted fusion. It tests whether a multimodal model with a different fusion method can match or beat 0.678. 3) Whether to use images at all is the biggest open design choice and could unlock the highest accuracy. Settling it now, while six runs remain, leaves budget either to refine multimodal settings or, if it fails, to go back and tune the RNA-only scGPT setup (aggregation, single vs multiprofile).

1) Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only scGPT with multiprofile transformer aggregation (config_006, accuracy 0.678, F1 0.646). scGPT clearly beats scVI in the RNA-only setting (0.678 vs 0.494). Adding ViT-L image features has hurt in both multimodal runs, with concat dropping scGPT to 0.532 and weighted fusion dropping scVI to 0.208. The main open question is whether transformer aggregation is the right choice for the strongest RNA-only scGPT setup. 2) Test: config_015 keeps scGPT, RNA-only and multiprofile fixed and changes only aggregation from transformer to avgpool. This is a clean single-factor comparison. 3) Why now: it builds on the strongest branch and could improve on 0.678, since simpler pooling may generalize better. Either way, it settles the aggregation choice for later experiments, such as single-profile scGPT or ResNet50-based multimodal runs. That makes it a better use of the budget than exploring the image-modality options that have so far underperformed.

1) Evidence: scGPT is clearly the strongest RNA encoder, well ahead of scVI. RNA-only scGPT scored 0.678 with transformer aggregation and 0.706 with avgpool, the current best. Adding images has hurt every time so far (0.532 with concat, 0.208 with scVI and weighted fusion). Every completed run has used the multiprofile setting, so the profile setting is still a complete unknown. 2) This experiment runs RNA-only scGPT with singleprofile. It tells us whether aggregating multiple profiles helps at all, or whether a simpler single-profile model matches or beats the 0.706 best. 3) Profile setting is the main untested design choice, and it sits on the strongest branch we have, so the result can either set a new best or confirm that multiprofile with avgpool is the right base. That is more useful now than another multimodal run, given that image fusion has consistently degraded results.

1) Evidence: The best result so far is RNA-only with the scGPT encoder (0.72 accuracy, single-profile). scGPT clearly beats scVI (0.68 vs 0.49 under matched RNA-only transformer settings). Within scGPT, simpler setups do slightly better: single-profile beats avgpool, which beats transformer. Adding ViT-L image features hurt in both runs that tried it, under concat and weighted fusion. The PCA_n2000 RNA encoder is still completely untested, and it is the largest remaining unknown in the most promising RNA-only branch. 2) Test: Run PCA_n2000 in the current best setting (RNA-only, single-profile). This is a direct comparison of encoders with everything else held fixed. A simple high-dimensional PCA representation can be competitive with or better than foundation-model embeddings. 3) Why now: With 3 experiments left, this cheaply settles which RNA encoder is best within the strongest branch. If PCA wins, the remaining budget can go to PCA variants. If it loses, scGPT is confirmed and the remaining runs can probe whether ResNet50 image features help, as a low-priority check given that adding image features has hurt so far.

1) Evidence: scGPT is clearly the strongest RNA encoder (0.68–0.72, versus 0.49–0.51 for scVI and PCA). For scGPT, single-profile and avgpool beat transformer aggregation; the best result so far is config_032 (scGPT, RNA-only, single-profile, 0.721). All remaining RNA-only options use the weaker encoders, so they are unlikely to beat 0.721. The only realistic way to improve is adding images to an scGPT single-profile model. Image fusion has hurt so far, but only ViT-L has been tested, and only with multi-profile transformer aggregation. ResNet50 is completely untested. 2) This experiment adds ResNet50 images to the best setting (scGPT, single-profile) using weighted fusion. Weighted fusion can in principle learn to downweight a weak image branch, which concat cannot. This changes two things at once (image encoder and fusion type), so a result will not cleanly separate their effects. That trade-off is accepted because the goal is the best score, not attribution. 3) With 2 experiments left, this is the most plausible candidate to beat 0.721 and the cleanest test of whether images help at all. If it helps, the final run can vary the fusion type or try ViT-L in the same setup. If it hurts, the remaining budget can go to the other single-profile scGPT multimodal variants (ViT-L, or concat fusion).

1) Evidence: scGPT is clearly the strongest RNA encoder, and singleprofile RNA-only scGPT (config_032, 0.721 acc) is the current best. Every scGPT RNA-only variant has now been tested, so any further gain has to come from multimodal scGPT. Multimodal runs have so far underperformed. The best of them is singleprofile scGPT + ResNet50 with weighted fusion (config_003, 0.579). Weighted fusion also produced a near-collapse in config_007 (0.208), so the fusion mechanism may be part of the problem. 2) Test: config_016 keeps config_003's strongest multimodal setup (singleprofile, scGPT, ResNet50) and changes only the fusion from weighted to concat. This shows whether concat fusion lets the image branch help, or at least stop hurting, the strong scGPT signal. 3) Why now: with only two experiments left, a single-variable change to the best multimodal setup is both a clean read on an open design choice (fusion type) and the multimodal candidate most likely to approach or beat the RNA-only best. If it does well, it points the final experiment toward the best image encoder or fusion combination.

1. Evidence: scGPT is clearly the strongest RNA encoder. The best result so far is RNA-only single-profile scGPT at 0.721 accuracy, followed by multiprofile avgpool at 0.706. Every scGPT RNA-only setting has now been tested. Adding images has hurt so far, but the least damaging setup was ResNet50 with concat fusion (0.653 single-profile, versus 0.579 with weighted fusion). Test: this run combines the best choice on each axis, giving a multimodal scGPT + ResNet50 model with avgpool aggregation and concat fusion over multiple profiles. It asks whether avgpool aggregation lets the image signal add to scGPT rather than dilute it. 3. Why this is the best final use: it is the untested configuration with the most plausible chance of beating 0.721. The other RNA encoders (scVI, PCA) have been much weaker, and ViT-L setups look unpromising.

1) No experiments have been run yet, so there is no empirical evidence. 1) Evidence: config_050 (scVI RNA, ViT-L image, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion, multiprofile) is best at 0.706 accuracy and 0.667 F1. This suggests ViT-L image features carry much of the signal. 2) Test: config_013 runs image-only ViT-L with multiprofile avgpool, keeping the best-performing aggregation and image encoder. It tells us whether the RNA branch adds value or adds noise. 3) Why now: this is the most plausible remaining route to beating 0.715, and it settles an important modality question. The matching RNA-only ablation (config_032) can follow as experiment 9 if needed.

Evidence: the best result so far is image-only ViT-L with multiprofile avgpool (config_013, 0.725 acc, 0.685 F1). The best multimodal run, scVI + ViT-L with avgpool and concat fusion (config_012, 0.715), is slightly lower, so adding RNA has not clearly helped. Several choices look clearly worse: weighted fusion, ResNet50, single-profile input, and the scGPT and PCA RNA encoders. Transformer aggregation dropped sharply, but only in one multimodal concat run (config_024, 0.53). That single drop may come from interaction with fusion rather than from the aggregator itself. Question: does transformer aggregation help or hurt in the strongest setting, image-only ViT-L multiprofile? Why now: aggregation is the only important design axis not yet tested on the top setting. Every other remaining option changes a factor that has already been shown to hurt, so this is the most plausible chance to beat 0.725. It also tells the final experiment whether to refine around avgpool or transformer aggregation.

Evidence: the best result so far is image-only ViT-L with avgpool (0.725). Multimodal scVI + ViT-L with avgpool and concat is close behind (0.715). Transformer aggregation (about 0.53), weighted fusion (0.527), single-profile input (0.427) and ResNet50 (0.573) all clearly underperformed, so most untested configurations that use these choices are unlikely to win. The main unresolved question is how strong the RNA modality is alone, because RNA-only has never been tested. This experiment uses the strongest RNA encoder (scVI, which beat PCA and scGPT in multimodal runs) with the best aggregation (multiprofile avgpool). It checks whether RNA alone might match or exceed the image-only result, and whether concat fusion is diluting a strong RNA signal. With only this one experiment left, it is the only plausible candidate with real upside. The remaining image or multimodal options combine choices already shown to perform worse.

1. There is no experimental evidence yet. The main uncertainties are modality (multimodal vs. single-modality), profile setting, RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation and fusion. Prior knowledge suggests multimodal, multiprofile models with learned aggregation are likely strong, but that is only an expectation. 2. config_015 tests a strong prior candidate: multimodal, multiprofile, scVI RNA embeddings, ImageNet ViT-L image features, transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. Only the best accuracy within the budget counts, so starting with a likely strong configuration secures a good baseline early. 1) Evidence and uncertainty: we have one result. config_015 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI-200, ViT-L, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion) reached 0.328 accuracy and 0.288 F1. This isolates whether multiprofile input with transformer aggregation actually helps over single-profile prediction. 3) Why it is the best next use: profile setting is a structural choice that splits the search space roughly in half. 1. Evidence: The two runs share the same scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder and weighted fusion. Singleprofile reached 0.519 accuracy and 0.480 F1. Multiprofile with transformer aggregation reached only 0.328 accuracy and 0.288 F1. Because the multiprofile run used transformer aggregation, this gap mixes two factors: profile setting and aggregation method. A transformer aggregator may be poorly suited to this data. 2. Test: config_003 keeps every other setting the same and switches only the aggregation to avgpool. This shows whether multiprofile is worse in general or whether the transformer aggregator caused the drop. 3. Why now: This is the most important design question still open, because it decides whether half of the search space is worth exploring. 1. Evidence: All three runs used scVI RNA, ViT-L images and weighted fusion. Singleprofile is best (0.519 accuracy, 0.480 F1). Multiprofile with avgpool is slightly lower (0.494), and multiprofile with transformer is much worse (0.328). Test: This run swaps only the RNA encoder from scVI to scGPT and keeps every other setting from the best configuration. The result isolates whether the scGPT pretrained embeddings beat scVI. 3. Evidence: the single-profile multimodal configs lead. scGPT + ViT-L + weighted fusion (config_021) scored 0.523 acc / 0.508 F1, and the scVI version (config_035) scored 0.519 / 0.480. Multiprofile aggregation did worse, with avgpool at 0.494 and transformer at 0.328. RNA encoder choice made only a small difference in accuracy, though F1 favored scGPT. Because only one variable changes, the result is easy to attribute, and it exploits the best region while closing a major gap in our knowledge. Questions about image encoder and unimodal baselines can follow in the remaining budget.

1. Evidence: Single-profile with weighted fusion leads so far. scGPT (0.523) and scVI (0.519) score almost the same, so the RNA encoder looks like a minor factor. Weighted fusion beat concat (0.523 vs 0.485). Multiprofile with avgpool (0.494) and especially with transformer (0.328) did worse. The biggest open question is the image encoder: every run so far used imagenet_vit_l, and resnet50 has never been tried. 2. Test: config_034 keeps the best setup (single-profile, scGPT, weighted fusion) and swaps only the image encoder to resnet50, so any change can be attributed to the image encoder alone. 3. Why now: this resolves a design choice that has seen no testing, rather than refining choices already narrowed. If resnet50 wins, it opens a better region for the remaining three experiments. If it loses, we can commit to ViT-L and spend those three on the RNA encoder (e.g., PCA) or on improving multiprofile avgpool.

1. Evidence: Switching the image encoder from ViT-L to ResNet50 gave the largest gain so far, raising accuracy from 0.523 to 0.629 (config_034, F1 0.599). Singleprofile with weighted fusion has beaten multiprofile aggregation (avgpool 0.494, transformer 0.328) and concat fusion (0.485). scGPT and scVI performed almost the same with ViT-L, but the PCA RNA encoder has never been tested, so it is the largest remaining uncertainty. 2. Test: config_016 keeps the best context (singleprofile, ResNet50, weighted fusion) and swaps in PCA as the RNA encoder. Why now: It explores the only untested RNA encoder inside the strongest known region, so it has a real chance of beating 0.629. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_016 (multimodal, singleprofile, pca_n2000 + resnet50, weighted fusion) at 0.688 accuracy and 0.659 F1. The image encoder looks like the largest lever: switching from ViT-L to ResNet50 added about 0.105 accuracy with scGPT. Swapping scGPT for PCA added a smaller 0.06. Singleprofile has beaten multiprofile in every comparison, and weighted fusion beat concat. What remains untested is whether the RNA branch helps at all, since no unimodal baseline has been run. 2. Test: Image-only ResNet50 in the singleprofile setting isolates how much of the current performance comes from the image modality. If it matches or beats 0.688, RNA is adding noise and image-only may be the best configuration. If it falls well short, that confirms fusion is useful, and the last two experiments can refine the multimodal setup (e.g., the concat variant or the multiprofile avgpool version of the best encoders). 3. Why now: With two experiments left after this one, settling the modality question has high value. It could directly produce a new best, and it decides how to spend the rest of the budget. Small encoder or fusion tweaks around config_016 would only test variations the evidence already ranks below it.

Evidence: the best result so far is config_016 (single-profile, pca_n2000 RNA, ResNet50 image, weighted fusion) at 0.688 accuracy and 0.659 F1. ResNet50 has clearly beaten ViT-L (0.629 vs 0.523 with scGPT). Weighted fusion has beaten concat (0.523 vs 0.485). The main open question is profile aggregation. Multi-profile with a transformer did poorly (0.328). Multi-profile with avgpool was only slightly below single-profile (0.494 vs 0.519), and that was with the weaker scVI/ViT-L encoders. With only two experiments left, this extension of the best configuration has the most realistic chance of beating 0.688. Other options look less likely to win: swapping in scVI, trying concat, or running unimodal baselines.

1) Evidence: the clear best result is config_016 (singleprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, weighted fusion) at 0.688 accuracy and 0.659 F1. Singleprofile has beaten multiprofile in every comparison so far. ResNet50 beat ViT-L, and pca_n2000 beat scgpt when paired with resnet50. The only open question near the best setup is fusion. Concat underperformed weighted only once (scgpt + ViT-L, about 0.04 lower), which is weak evidence from a single pair. 2) This experiment keeps the best encoder pair and profile setting and swaps fusion to concat. Changing only the least-tested factor keeps the run close to the best configuration. The alternatives look less promising: scvi with resnet50 swaps in an RNA encoder that has not outperformed pca, and RNA-only drops the image signal that multimodal fusion clearly benefited from.

1) No experiments have been run, so every design choice is uncertain. Prior expectation is that multimodal, multiprofile models with learned aggregation are the strongest setting for cellular profiling. 2) config_013 tests a high-prior anchor: a multimodal multiprofile model with scVI RNA embeddings, an ImageNet ViT-L image encoder, transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. 1. Evidence: there is only one result so far. config_013 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI, ViT-L, transformer, weighted fusion) reached 0.435 accuracy and 0.423 F1. That is a reasonable baseline but says nothing yet about which design choices matter. 2. Test: config_014 keeps every setting the same except the RNA encoder, which changes from scVI to scGPT. Evidence: Holding everything else fixed (ViT-L images, transformer aggregation, weighted fusion), switching the RNA encoder from scVI to scGPT raised validation accuracy from 0.435 to 0.537, with F1 moving in step. 1. Evidence: the best result so far is config_007 (scGPT, ViT-L, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. Switching fusion from weighted to concat raised accuracy by about 0.18. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_007 (scGPT + ViT-L + transformer + concat, accuracy 0.721). Two design choices look clear. Concat beat weighted fusion by about 0.18 under the same encoders. ViT-L beat ResNet50 by about 0.39 under concat. Transformer aggregation also beat avgpool under weighted fusion. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_007 (scGPT + ViT-L, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. The other axes are fairly consistent. 1. Evidence: config_007 (scGPT + ViT-L + transformer + concat) leads at 0.721 accuracy and 0.681 F1. The other results point the same way. Concat beat weighted fusion by about 0.18. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_007 (scGPT + ViT-L, transformer, concat) at 0.721 accuracy. Each factor has a fairly consistent effect. 1) Evidence: the best result so far is config_007 (scGPT + ViT-L, transformer aggregation, concat fusion, multiprofile) at 0.721 accuracy. Each single change from it lowered accuracy. 1) No experiments have been run yet, so there is no evidence on any design choice. My priors are that multimodal models beat unimodal ones, multiprofile aggregation helps, and the stronger ViT-L image encoder beats ResNet50, but none of this is tested. 2) config_043 combines all of these: multimodal, multiprofile, scVI RNA embeddings, ViT-L image encoder, transformer aggregation and weighted fusion. 1. Evidence: The best result is rna_only + multiprofile + scvi_n200 + transformer at 0.629 accuracy. 1. Evidence: there is only one result so far. The multimodal setup (scVI + ViT-L, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) reached 0.507 accuracy and 0.455 F1. We do not yet know how much of that comes from the image branch versus the RNA branch. 2. Test: config_003 is the RNA-only version of the same setup, with the same scVI encoder, transformer aggregation and multiprofile setting. 1. Evidence: The RNA encoder is the only factor varied so far. pca_n2000 (0.725 acc / 0.685 F1) clearly beats scvi_n200 (0.540) and scgpt (0.485) when everything else is held fixed (multiprofile, ViT-L, transformer, concat). 1. Evidence: pca_n2000 is the clear best RNA encoder so far (0.725 accuracy vs 0.540 for scvi_n200 and 0.485 for scgpt, all with ViT-L, transformer and concat). Concat fusion beat weighted fusion by a wide margin (0.725 vs 0.260) in the only head-to-head comparison. Aggregation has not been varied at all: every run used the transformer. 2. Evidence: the best result so far is config_049 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + concat) at 0.725 accuracy and 0.685 F1. Changing the RNA encoder to scvi or scgpt cost 0.19 to 0.24 accuracy. Switching to avgpool aggregation cost 0.09, and weighted fusion collapsed to 0.26. So the RNA encoder, aggregation and fusion choices are reasonably settled. The image encoder is still completely untested, since every run so far used vit_l. Evidence: the RNA encoder drives most of the variance in results. pca_n2000 reached about 0.72, while scvi scored 0.54 and scgpt 0.48. Swapping the image encoder from ViT-L to ResNet50 barely changed accuracy (0.725 vs 0.715), so the image branch may add little. If it scores lower, it confirms multimodal fusion is worth keeping, and the remaining runs can focus on refining the pca/transformer/concat multimodal family.

1) Evidence: Every run so far has been multiprofile. Swapping in scVI or scGPT, avgpool or weighted fusion all hurt accuracy, and RNA-only (0.512) confirms that adding images helps. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_049 (PCA-2000 + ViT-L, transformer, concat, multiprofile) at 0.725 accuracy. Swapping the image encoder to ResNet50 gives nearly the same score (0.715). 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_049 (pca_n2000 + ViT-L + transformer + concat) at 0.725 accuracy. 1. Evidence: The RNA encoder matters most so far. pca_n2000 (0.706 to 0.715) clearly beats scgpt (0.530) and scvi_n200 (0.507). 1) Evidence: config_049 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI, ViT-L, transformer, concat) is the clear best at 0.713 accuracy with matching F1. 1. Evidence: We have only one result. config_044 (multimodal, multiprofile, scVI-200, ResNet50, avgpool, concat) reached 0.494 validation accuracy and 0.453 F1. 1) Evidence and uncertainty: the best result is config_016 at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1, using scvi_n200 RNA, a resnet50 image encoder, avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion. 1) Evidence: the best result so far is config_016 (scVI + ResNet50, avgpool, weighted fusion) at 0.713 accuracy and 0.695 F1. Every axis we varied away from it lowered accuracy. My prior is that combining modalities (multimodal) and aggregating over multiple profiles (multiprofile) are the settings most likely to reach high validation accuracy. 2. What this tests: config_004 sets a strong mid-complexity anchor. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_006 (pca_n2000 + imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) at 0.635 accuracy and 0.618 F1. Several design choices look settled. Transformer aggregation clearly beats avgpool (0.62 vs 0.52 for scgpt/vit_l). Concat fusion beats weighted fusion (0.62 vs 0.59 for scgpt, 0.64 vs 0.47 for pca). imagenet_vit_l beats resnet50 (0.64 vs 0.59 for pca). The RNA encoder matters less than the image encoder, and RNA-only with pca reached just 0.33. That pattern suggests most of the signal comes from the ViT-L image features. The remaining multimodal options are unlikely to beat config_006: scgpt+resnet50 concat combines a weaker RNA encoder with the weaker image encoder, singleprofile drops the aggregation that appears important, and the other options use avgpool or weighted fusion. 2) Test: config_001 (image-only, imagenet_vit_l, multiprofile, transformer) checks whether the RNA branch adds real value or partly adds noise. The large drops seen with weighted fusion hint that adding RNA does not always help. If the RNA branch is diluting the image signal, image-only could match or exceed the current best. Either way, it fills the most important missing piece of the comparison: the image-only baseline. 3) Why this last slot: it is the most plausible remaining route to a higher score, and it is also informative. Expected cost is low, likely about 2-3 GPU hours (single modality, no fusion), which is below the roughly 4-7 hours of the multimodal runs.

1) No experiments have been run, so there is no evidence on which modality setting, profile setting, encoders, aggregation or fusion work best. 1) Evidence: The best result so far is config_024 (scVI + ViT-L, transformer aggregation, concat fusion) at 0.706 accuracy and 0.667 F1. Every single-factor deviation from it scored lower. 1. Evidence: The best result so far is config_024 at 0.706 accuracy (scVI + ViT-L, multimodal multiprofile, transformer aggregation, concat fusion). Four design choices clearly matter. Expected cost: it drops image processing, so it should be well below config_009's 36 GPU hours.
